compile_schedule.rule: place arith_start (io_word[470], IO stripe 2 bit 26) ARITH_START_ADVANCE_R10 = 1 IO row EARLIER than for r7c; every other IO field unchanged
compile_schedule.effect: compiler_control and programme_active/done/ordinal then reach the core on the r7c edge; io_word, IO status and D=4 unchanged; 0 cycles per token
compile_schedule.constraint: arith_start row >= 1 (the canonical Qswiglu schedule has it at row 210 + 2*LG_PATH)
compile_schedule.host_contract: start (io_start_v) >= 4 edges after the last configuration write (unchanged)

fault_semantics: a faulting stripe zeroes its own outputs at once and the sticky store fault raises `fault` (programme-stripe faults 1 edge after r7c, IO faults on the r7c edge); stripes that have not faulted keep emitting their words until the host acts on `fault` (r7c zeroed all stripes); the host must not launch again after a fault (as r7c)
